fix(server): the job may set the store's async commit (#2802)

Part of #2802. The game half of opensro-ops#287.

## Change

`SRO_STORE_ASYNC_COMMIT` joins `NotSettings` in `internal/config/shardsettings`. It picks the store's write path (the async commit writer, `internal/data/store/commit_writer.go`), not a rule a player plays by, so it is not a shard-setting row and does not reach the catalogue.

## Why now

The owner decided on 2026-11-11 to turn the writer on with the next release; ops #287 adds the job variable. The job contract is checked both ways (`TestEveryJobSettingIsListed`: every `SRO_` variable the job sets is a Settings row or a NotSettings entry, and every NotSettings entry is still in the job). Without this entry ops #287 fails that check; with it, ops main is red until #287 lands, so the two land back to back.

## Tests

`go test ./internal/config/shardsettings` with ops #287's `server-ops` laid in as `apps/server/ops`: pass.

Player-note: Server: no visible change; the save's disk write moves off the lock the game waits on.

Old-tab: safe - server-only table entry: no wire frame, opcode or client code changes.

## Native claims

none - a deployment table entry for a port-only store mechanism.

test(e2e): wait for the board to mount before driving Clear filters

Closes https://github.com/alrayyes/forge-dashboard/issues/3472

## Cause

A spec race, not an app bug. The page ships its filter inputs in the served HTML and attaches the handlers when the script mounts. The Clear filters specs filled the title box right after `goto`, so under load the input event could land before the handler existed. The button then stayed disabled (or the follow-up click timed out).

With a deliberate 400 ms delay on every `.js` response, 4 of the 6 specs failed on every run. The ticket's "re-render replaced the button" guess did not hold: the button is never replaced.

## Fix

`beforeEach`, the issues-page spec and the reload spec now wait for the "Refreshed" label to be visible. It only shows after the first load, which happens after mount. No timeouts changed, assertions unchanged.

## Counts

- Before (16 workers, `--repeat-each=40`, 16 CPU hogs): 10 of 240 failed.
- After (16 workers, `--repeat-each=50`, 16 CPU hogs): 0 of 300 failed.
- After, with the 400 ms probe: 6 of 6 pass.
- Whole `dashboard.spec.ts` plus the two filter-choices specs: 130 passed.

Other specs that fill straight after `goto` may have the same race (see #3463).

fix(client): a corrected run turns onto the corrected line instead of sliding sideways (#3148)

## What

Issue #3148 (report BR-261110-0255-3F01): while running, a server correction of 3-8 units made the character slide sideways like a car instead of running cleanly to the corrected line. The requests were accepted and the character ended in the right place; only the presentation of each correction drifted.

The own-walk presenter recovers a correction by keeping the drawn body where it stood and decaying the difference while the corrected walk runs on underneath. The body therefore travels diagonally to the corrected line, but its nose kept the old bearing, so for the length of the recovery (measured: ~0.6 s for a 5-unit sideways shift at 100 u/s) up to half the run speed was sideways slide under a fixed nose (46 u/s across the facing, nose deviation 0 degrees).

## Change

`own-walk-interpolation.ts` only. While a correction's offset is still being given back on a moving walk, the presenter now faces the bearing of the step it is actually drawing (the existing `movementHeading`), turned at the presenter's native heading rate, so the body turns onto the corrected line and settles back onto the line's bearing as the offset drains. The interpolation buffer reports the recovery (`correcting()`), and the first frame after a correction still stands where the body stood, so nothing jumps. The drawn positions are computed exactly as before - same path, same settle, same speed cap; only the facing during recovery changes. At rest the worker's heading rules throughout, so the pinned stop-correction glide and the teleport snap are untouched. This presenter is port-only smoothing (owner's 2026-10-24 ruling in the file header), so no native default changes and no flag is added.

Measured on a replayed corrected run (100 u/s, +5 units sideways): before, nose deviation 0 degrees with a 46 u/s sideways peak; after, the nose turns ~19 degrees onto the run and tracks the drawn step's bearing within a frame, settling on the corrected line at the same moment as before. Same at 8 units and at -5.

## Tests

New regression test in `own-walk-interpolation.test.mjs`: a corrected run (the report's correction size) at the recording's frame pattern asserts the 1.05 speed bar, that the nose turns at least 10 degrees toward the corrected line, that the sideways share of the drawn step stays under 30% of run speed once the turn has had four frames, and that the body settles on the corrected line with its nose back on bearing. It fails on the old code ("the nose turned 0 words toward the line") and passes now. Existing suites: `own-walk-interpolation` 13/13, the movement correction/reaim/stale-arrival family 31/31, pose presentation suites 115/115, `verify:quick` green, dprint clean.

Player-note: Animation: A run the server corrects now turns onto the corrected line instead of drifting sideways.

Old-tab: safe - presentation-only change inside the client; no wire, protocol or persisted shape moves, and an older tab simply keeps the previous facing behaviour.

## Native claims

| Claim | Evidence | How checked | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No native behaviour is claimed or changed: the correction smoothing is port-only (file header, owner 2026-10-24), and this change only picks which bearing the drawn body faces while a correction offset drains; the heading turn applied is the port's existing native-rate turn already used for every drawn frame. | `own-walk-interpolation.ts` header and the presenter wiring in `pose-presentation.ts` | Diff read; the drawn positions and settle assertions of the existing suite are unchanged and green | Confirmed (report) |

fix: Use the default value of variables set to null

## Description

Closes #98

Variables with a default value accepted `null`, which either broke the plan or silently changed the purge function's behaviour:

- `purge_schedule = null` created the cron trigger with a null schedule, and the plan failed with "Missing required argument".
- `purge_preserve_tag_patterns = null` made `join()` fail in `functions.tf`. This case isn't listed in #98, but is fixed the same way.
- `purge_dry_run`, `purge_retention_days` and `purge_log_level` set to `null` passed the plan, but the function received an empty environment variable and fell back to dry-run mode or the `Info` level at runtime.

Change: `nullable = false` on `is_public` and every `purge_*` variable. Terraform now uses their default value when they are set to `null`. Note that `purge_schedule = null` therefore means the default schedule: `purge_schedule = ""` remains the way to disable the cron trigger.

Tested locally with Terraform 1.14.0 and mock providers: setting these variables to `null` failed the plan before the change, and falls back to their defaults after it. `terraform fmt`, `terraform validate` and `tflint` pass, and `terraform-docs .` leaves the README unchanged.

## AI usage

- [x] AI was used, and every commit containing AI-produced work ends with a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer naming it.

Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`) in Claude Code wrote the change and ran the checks listed above.

## Checklist

- [x] I have reviewed, understood and tested every change in this pull request, and I take responsibility for it.
- [x] Terraform code (if applicable): `terraform fmt`, `terraform validate` and `tflint` pass locally.
- [x] Terraform modules (if applicable): the documentation block of `README.md` is up to date (`terraform-docs .`).

fix(web): make the rebase-all dialog list keyboard scrollable

The rebase-all dialog's list scrolls (`max-height: 40vh`, `overflow-y: auto`) but had no tab stop, so a keyboard user couldn't reach the rows below the fold before confirming. axe flagged `scrollable-region-focusable` on `#rebase-all-list`.

When the list overflows, `openRebaseAll` now sets `tabindex=0` and an `aria-label` ("Pull requests to rebase (N)"). The CSS gives it an inset focus ring so the dialog doesn't clip it. A list that fits gets neither, so it isn't an extra stop. Reproduced on current main first: the four new overflow cases were red there.

Deviation from the Stitch note: I kept it a `ul` with a name rather than adding `role=region`, since that would drop the list and listitem semantics the existing tests and screen readers rely on.

Tests: new cases in `tests/bot-rebase-all.spec.ts` (already registered) at 320 and 390 wide, light and dark: tab stop, name, Tab cycle, visible outline, PageDown scrolls, axe clean; plus a non-overflowing list has no tabindex.

Not done: the before/after screenshots from the ticket's DoD, so this is `Refs`, not `Closes`; the ticket stays open for them.

Refs https://github.com/alrayyes/forge-dashboard/issues/3402

fix(case): start the plugin tools with a PATH so dmidecode and ethtool are found

After a reboot, the Case page's Inside view on the DXP4800 GT drew both RAM slots as empty, and the maximum LAN speed was missing.

Cause: `web/plugin/api.php` `run()` and `fan_profile.php` start the tools with `proc_open(..., [])`, an empty environment, so there is no PATH. A bare `dmidecode` (`/usr/sbin`) and `ethtool` are not found and `hardware` returns `"memory": null`. A good result is cached in tmpfs, so the view only worked once something with a normal PATH (for example `diag` from a shell) had read the memory first, and stopped working after every reboot.

Fix: one `TOOL_ENV` with a standard PATH for both `proc_open` calls. The `shell_exec` and `exec` calls go through `sh`, which sets its own default PATH. Adds a parser test with the tower's dmidecode output (two SODIMMs, both locator `DIMM 0`, banks `P0 CHANNEL A/B`; no serials).

Verified on the tower (read-only, private mount namespace with an empty `/var/run` tmpfs): `env -i ugreen-nas-fan hardware` returns `"memory": null`; with the new PATH both modules come back.

Not run: the installed page itself; `just check` (nix dev shell won't build on this Mac because of zizmor). gofmt, `go vet`, `go test ./internal/fan`, `php -l` and php-cs-fixer ran directly.

新建失败不再指向旧日志，README 版本提示改指 Releases，MODAVD_TEST_TMP 下测试能建目录

## 为什么

ModAVD/ModAVD#174 记下的三处小问题，都不影响使用。

## 改了什么

**新建在开机前就失败时，报错指向旧日志**

`modavd create` 在拉起模拟器之前就失败（比如根目录缺 adb）时，这次没有日志，`newestEmulatorLog` 取到的是这个编号以前留下的旧日志。现在它只取这次新建开始以后写的日志（留 2 秒余量），没有就不附「日志见」，也不记 `creationLog`。`--resume` 关残留实例失败时，照旧取残留那次开机的日志。

**README 的版本提示过期**

`README.md`、`README.en.md` 第 9 行还写着 `main` 是 0.3.0、最新 Release 是 v0.1.0。改成：本文按 `main` 写，可能有还没发版的改动，已发布的版本见 Releases 页。

**设了 `MODAVD_TEST_TMP` 时有测试建不出目录**

`internal/report` 的 `testTempDir` 把子测试名直接当目录名，名字里的 `"`、`:` 在 Windows 上不合法，`TestDiagnosticCollectBadMetadataReported` 因此失败。现在把 `<>:"/\|?*` 和控制字符换成 `_`。

## 测试

- 新单测 `TestCreateFailureLogIsThisAttempts`：有两天前的旧日志、开机前失败时不附日志；这次写了新日志时附的是新日志。去掉修复时失败。
- 设 `MODAVD_TEST_TMP` 跑 `TestDiagnosticCollectBadMetadataReported`：修复前失败，修复后通过。
- `go test ./internal/emu/... ./internal/report/...` 通过，`go vet` 通过。

Refs ModAVD/ModAVD#174

platform-tools 是目录联接时也认得出自己起的 logcat 采集

## 为什么

根目录的 `sdk\platform-tools` 是目录联接或符号链接时，管理器认不出自己起的 logcat 采集：开机不打印 `logcat：<路径>`，开诊断模式误报「已有其它程序采集 logcat」（ModAVD/ModAVD#135）。

原因是 `capturePathMatches` 在 Windows 上只比路径名：进程映像路径是解析过链接的，`m.Root.AdbExe()` 是经过链接的，两边对不上。根目录本身是联接时，`tools\modavd.exe` 和根目录参数的比对也一样。

## 改了什么

`internal/emu/capture_policy.go` 的 `capturePathMatches`：Windows 上名字（不分大小写）一样就算；不一样时再按文件身份（`os.SameFile`）比，和其它平台的做法一样。`ownedCapture`、`pendingOwnedCapture`、`waitDiagnosticCaptureRuntime`、`ownsCaptureHelper` 都经过它，一起修好。

## 测试

- 新单测 `TestCapturePathMatchesThroughJunction`：`platform-tools` 是目录联接、根目录是联接、大小写不同、同目录的别的文件、不存在的文件、空路径。去掉修复时前两项失败。
- `go test ./internal/emu/...` 通过；`go vet`（Windows、`GOOS=darwin`）通过。

Refs ModAVD/ModAVD#135
